title: Install and get started
description: Install XShot, allow screen access, and take your first screenshot.
body:
XShot is a native macOS tool for screenshots and product demos. Set up the app and allow screen access, then start capturing or recording.

XShot currently uses Chinese interface labels. This English guide includes the on-screen Chinese labels alongside their English explanations.

Check the system requirements

XShot supports Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later.

Install from GitHub

  1. Download the XShot v0.2.0 DMG from GitHub.
  2. Open the DMG and drag XShot.app into Applications.
  3. Open XShot from Applications. You can eject the disk image after copying the app.

The app uses ad hoc signing and has no Apple notarization. If macOS blocks it, see how to open XShot.

Xcode Command Line Tools are needed only to build from source. You do not need developer tools to run an already built XShot.app.

Build from source

  1. If Xcode Command Line Tools are not installed, run xcode-select --install in Terminal and follow the system instructions.
  2. Get the source on GitHub. In Terminal, go to the source folder and run ./scripts/build.sh. You can also double-click Run XShot.command in the project folder.
  3. When the build finishes, drag dist/XShot.app into Applications.
  4. Open XShot from Applications or Spotlight.
git clone https://github.com/hijoebon/xshot.git
cd xshot
./scripts/build.sh

Before replacing an older version, finish any recording or export and quit XShot. Keep a complete backup of the demo projects you need.

Allow screen access

  1. Open XShot and click Screenshot (截图), or press ⌥X.
  2. Follow the permission prompt, or open System Settings → Privacy & Security.
  3. Allow XShot under Screen & System Audio Recording. Some macOS versions call this Screen Recording.
  4. Reopen the app when prompted. If capture still fails just after granting access, quit and reopen XShot, then try again.

The word “audio” in the system permission name does not mean XShot records sound. Recordings currently have no audio. You can still annotate local files with Open Image… (打开图片…) without screen access.

Take your first screenshot

  1. Press ⌥X. Click a highlighted window, or drag to select an area.
  2. To highlight a detail, choose an arrow, rectangle, or text and annotate directly inside the selection.
  3. Press Enter to copy and finish, then press ⌘V in the destination app. To save a PNG, press ⌘S.

Learn more about screenshots and annotations, or record a product demo. If macOS blocks the app, follow the steps for opening XShot.

title: Screenshots and annotations
description: Select a window or area, highlight what matters, then copy or save.
body:
There is no need to open the editor first. Choose a capture area, add annotations, and copy or save a screenshot that makes your point.

Capture a window, area, or display

  1. Press ⌥X, or choose Screenshot from the menu bar.
  2. Window: move over the target window and click when its outline is highlighted. Area: drag to select a region. Display: click Entire Screen (整个屏幕) or press ⌘A.
  3. To adjust the selection, drag inside it to move it, or drag an edge or corner to resize it. Arrow keys move it by 1 pixel; hold Shift to move by 10 pixels.

Press Esc to cancel. Area and display captures cover one display at a time. An independent window capture includes the full window at Retina pixel resolution, without the system’s outer shadow.

Add annotations

Choose Rectangle, Arrow, or Pen and set the color and line width. With the Text tool selected, click a blank spot and type. Press Return for a new line. Press ⌘Return or click outside the text box to finish. Double-click an existing text annotation to edit it again.

With Mosaic selected, drag to brush over the area you want to pixelate, or click for a single dab. Adjust the brush size independently. Each stroke can be undone with ⌘Z.

Press V and click an annotation to select it. Drag to move it, use the handles to resize it, or press Delete to remove it. The toolbar lets you change its color, line width, text size, or mosaic brush size where applicable.

Press ⌘Z to undo, ⇧⌘Z to redo, or ⇧⌘⌫ to clear all annotations. You can undo a clear.

Adding an annotation locks the selection. Clear the annotations before adjusting it again.

Copy or save a PNG

Press Enter / ⌘C, or click Copy (复制), to finish the capture. Use ⌘V to paste into a chat or document. Press ⌘S or click Save (保存) to choose where to save a PNG. Canceling the save dialog returns you to the selection and annotations.

To style or pin the screenshot, click Editor (编辑器) or press ⇧⌘E. Your annotations and undo history carry over. The default Light Shadow style also applies when copying or saving directly; see screenshot styling to remove it.

Annotate an existing image

Click Open Image… (打开图片…) or press ⌘O, then choose a PNG, JPEG, TIFF, HEIC, or BMP file. Opening a local image does not automatically replace your clipboard contents. Copy or save it when you are ready. Editing a local image does not require screen access.

See the keyboard shortcut reference for tools and colors. Scrolling screenshots and OCR are not currently supported.

title: Screenshot styling and pinning
description: Add padding, rounded corners, and backgrounds, or keep a reference image on your desktop.
body:
Prepare a clean screenshot to share, or keep important information on your desktop for reference. The style you choose applies to both exported images and pinned images.

Add padding and rounded corners

  1. In the editor, click Styling (美化) or press ⇧⌘B.
  2. Choose Original (原图), Light Shadow (轻影), Padding (留白), or Showcase (展示). You can also adjust the background, padding, corner radius, shadow, and fine border individually.
  3. Check the canvas and the output dimensions shown at the bottom, then copy, save, or pin the image.

The initial default is Light Shadow: a transparent background, 24 px padding, 12 px corner radius, a soft shadow, and a fine border. Background options include transparent, white, mist gray, dark gray, and a blue gradient.

Padding is exported at the value you choose. A value of 0 px adds no margin. Shadows extending beyond the canvas are clipped. Transparent backgrounds may appear against different colors in other apps.

Return to the original image

Under Styling (美化), choose Original (原图) or Restore Original (恢复原图). This turns off styling while keeping the source image and your annotations.

To change just one image, adjust it in the editor. To change the style of future screenshots, update the defaults.

Pin an image to the desktop

In the editor, click Pin (贴图) or press ⇧⌘P. You can move and zoom pinned images and keep several open at once.

  • The floating controls at the bottom right offer Copy, Save, and More.
  • Right-click or choose More (更多) to select 100% / 50% / Fit to Window, change opacity, or close the image.
  • Use the menu bar to hide or show all pinned images together.

Set your default style

Press ⌘, to open Settings. Adjust the default image style, annotation color, line width, and Copy Automatically When Opening the Capture Editor (进入截图编辑器时自动复制). Changes save automatically and persist after restarting.

The defaults apply to direct output from a selection and newly opened editors. Individual adjustments to images already open are kept. Restore Defaults (恢复默认设置) returns to Light Shadow, red annotations, a 4 px line width, and automatic copying.

title: Record a product demo
description: Record one workflow, then create a video with automatic zoom and a clickable walkthrough.
body:
Start with a real workflow. XShot saves video, pointer movement, and clicks on your Mac, then lets you edit the demo video and interactive steps separately.

Choose what to record

  1. Press ⌥R or click Product Demo (产品演示).
  2. Choose Screen / Window / Area (屏幕 / 窗口 / 区域), check the preview, and name the project.
  3. Choose no countdown, 3 seconds, or 5 seconds, then click Start Recording (开始录制). When the countdown finishes, use the target app as usual.

Record one display, one independent window, or an area within one display at a time. Source recordings are up to 1920 px wide, with a target frame rate of up to 60 fps. XShot’s own windows are excluded from capture.

Microphone audio, system audio, and a camera overlay are not currently included. Before recording, silence notifications, tidy the desktop, and check for private information.

Pause, finish, or record again

  • Pause / resume: press ⌥P or use the recording controller. Paused time does not count toward the recording, and pointer data and steps are not captured while paused.
  • Finish: press ⌥R or click Finish (完成) to save the local project and open the demo editor.
  • Record again: use Record Again (重新录制) in the controller. The previous take is saved as a separate project before a new recording starts.

Edit the video and its zoom

  1. Switch to Demo Video (演示视频) and play it to check the workflow.
  2. Under Retained Range (保留范围), move to the desired playback position and click Set In Point (设为入点) or Set Out Point (设为出点) to trim the beginning or end. Choose Restore Full Video (恢复整段) when needed.
  3. Select a zoom segment on the left to adjust its start, end, zoom level, or enabled state. Click Set Focus in Preview (在画面中定位), then choose the area to emphasize.
  4. Turn off Automatic Focus (自动聚焦), Show Pointer (显示鼠标), or Click Indicators (点击提示) if needed, then preview before exporting.

Automatic focus plans zooms around clicks and groups nearby consecutive clicks into a stable focal area. Trimming changes only the video’s retained range; the original recording and interactive steps remain available.

Create a clickable walkthrough

  1. Switch to Interactive Steps (交互步骤). Review each screenshot taken before a click, along with the final result image.
  2. Replace generic titles such as “步骤 1” (“Step 1”) and their descriptions with the actual action and purpose.
  3. Click or drag a hotspot to reposition it, choose its destination step, and add, remove, or reorder steps as needed.
  4. Switch to Preview (预览) and click through the path yourself, checking branches, back navigation, and completion.

Interactive steps use screenshots and hotspots. They do not operate the real product or clone a web page’s DOM. There are currently no AI-written workflow descriptions, so edit the text before sharing. Next, see exports and local projects.

Current recording limits

Capture one display, an independent window, or an area within one display. Recording multiple displays at once is not supported. Source recordings are up to 1920 px wide, with a target frame rate of up to 60 fps. Microphone audio, system audio, and camera capture are not currently supported.

Automatic step screenshots are capped at 200. Very fast actions, insufficient cached frames before a click, or heavy write activity can leave some step images missing. The original video and click data are still retained. Review the steps before export, and add the titles, descriptions, or screenshots you need.

title: Exports and local projects
description: Choose MP4 or offline HTML, and keep the project for future edits.
body:
Export a video for someone to watch, or an HTML file for them to click through at their own pace. Keep the original project if you want to make changes later.

Choose the right format

PurposeFormatWhere to find it
Watch the complete workflowMP4 videoDemo Video (演示视频) → Export… (导出…)
Click through the stepsOffline HTMLInteractive Steps (交互步骤) → Export… (导出…)
Continue editing later.xshotdemo projectKeep the complete project package

Export an MP4 video

  1. Under Demo Video (演示视频), check the retained range and zoom effects.
  2. Click Export… (导出…), choose a destination, and save.
  3. Wait for the export to finish, then open the MP4 to check the result.

MP4 exports use H.264, retain the source recording’s dimensions, and output a fixed 60 fps. Source recordings are up to 1920 px wide. Audio is not currently included.

You can cancel an export without losing the original recording or project. An existing file with the same name is replaced only after the new export succeeds.

Export offline HTML

  1. Under Interactive Steps (交互步骤), review the titles, descriptions, hotspots, and destinations.
  2. Switch to Preview (预览) and click through the walkthrough.
  3. Click Export… (导出…) to save the HTML file. Open it in a browser to check it before sharing.

Images, text, and the player are embedded in a single HTML file. It plays offline without a server. Hotspots only change the current demo step; they do not connect to or operate the software shown.

The HTML file is for playback. To make changes, open the original .xshotdemo project, edit it, and export again.

Find and reopen a project

Projects are saved by default in ~/Movies/XShot/, inside your Movies folder. In Finder, press ⇧⌘G and enter this path to open it.

演示 date-identifier.xshotdemo/
  recording.mov   Original video
  project.json    Click, zoom, and editing data
  steps/          Step screenshots

Open a project from Recent Projects (最近项目) on the recording setup screen, choose Open Demo Project… (打开演示项目…), or press ⇧⌘O. Demo edits save automatically. When moving or backing up a project, keep the entire package and all its contents.

MP4, HTML, and PNG exports are saved to the destination you choose. See local data and privacy for what to check before sharing.

body:

Tool shortcuts work when a selection or canvas is active. Click the editor canvas first if needed. While entering text, letters, numbers, and symbols work as normal typing. If another app has claimed a global shortcut, use the menu bar or recording controller.

title: Troubleshooting and FAQs
description: Get help with opening the app, screen access, screenshot styles, and recording.
body:
Find the symptom that matches your issue below. If it persists, report your macOS version, XShot version, steps to reproduce, and the full message in GitHub Issues.

macOS blocks the app

If macOS says the developer cannot be verified or Apple cannot check the app for malicious software, first confirm that the app came from source code or a distribution channel you trust. Then use the system’s exception process:

  1. Try to open XShot, then dismiss the warning.
  2. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security and find Open Anyway next to the relevant warning.
  3. Check the app name and follow the system instructions to open it.

If the warning says the app is damaged, will damage your computer, or poses another security risk, obtain a fresh copy from a trusted source or build from source. If it still fails, report the full message. Do not assume every warning is a permission issue. You do not need to disable Gatekeeper or clear all of the app’s extended attributes.

For the system’s instructions, see Apple: Safely open apps on your Mac.

Screenshots or recordings have no picture

  1. Check that XShot has screen recording access in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
  2. If you just granted access, quit and reopen the app.
  3. After reinstalling or replacing XShot, make sure the permission entry matches the copy you are using, then try a screenshot or short recording.

Without screen access, you can still annotate local files with Open Image… (打开图片…). See allowing screen access for the full steps.

A shortcut does not respond

Another app may have claimed the global shortcut. Try the menu bar to capture or open Product Demo, and use the controller to pause recording. Annotation shortcuts need an active selection or canvas. They do not switch tools while you are entering text.

Screenshot and editor questions

Why does my copied screenshot have padding and a shadow?

Light Shadow (轻影) is enabled by default. In Styling (美化), choose Original (原图) to turn it off. To change future screenshots, press ⌘, and update the default style in Settings.

Why can’t I adjust the selection?

Adding an annotation locks the selection. Clear annotations to adjust it again; clearing can be undone. To change an annotation within the existing area, press V and select it.

Why does pasting after opening an image still paste my previous content?

Opening a local image does not automatically replace the clipboard. Click Copy (复制) or press ⌘C in the editor, then paste into the destination app.

Recording and export questions

Why is there no sound in my video?

XShot currently records picture only, without microphone or system audio. The word “audio” in the system permission name does not add audio recording support.

Why do the steps have generic titles such as “步骤 1” (“Step 1”)?

XShot saves screenshots and hotspots from clicks, but does not currently interpret the workflow. Edit the titles and descriptions under Interactive Steps (交互步骤), then preview before sharing.

Can an exported HTML demo operate the real app?

No. It is a screenshot-based walkthrough, and hotspots only move between demo steps. Open the original .xshotdemo project to continue editing.

Are OCR, scrolling screenshots, or cloud sharing supported?

OCR, scrolling screenshots, cloud sharing, camera overlays, AI-written step descriptions, and automatic masking of sensitive information in recordings are not currently supported. Mosaic is a manual screenshot annotation tool.

What to include in a bug report

Include your Mac chip, macOS and XShot versions, what you did before the issue, and the exact error text. Check screenshots and recordings for private information before attaching them. Do not publish account details, customer data, or tokens from a project.

title: Local data and privacy
description: Understand screen access, where projects are stored, and what to check before sharing.
body:
XShot currently captures, records, and edits demos on your Mac. Original video, pointer movement, clicks, and step screenshots are stored in local projects. There is no account, subscription, or cloud-sharing workflow.

Why screen access is needed

Screenshot capture and recording require macOS screen access. XShot reads the screen when you start a screenshot, preview a recording source, or record. You can manage or revoke access in System Settings → Privacy & Security.

You can annotate local images without screen access. Recordings currently include no microphone or system audio, and keyboard input is not collected. Pointer positions and clicks during recording are used for automatic focus and step hotspots.

See allowing screen access for setup. The system permission may include “audio” in its name; this does not mean XShot records sound.

Where files are stored

ContentLocation
PNG screenshots, MP4, and HTMLThe location you choose when saving or exporting
Original demo video and editing dataA .xshotdemo project package, in ~/Movies/XShot/ by default
Default styling, annotation, and automatic-copy settingsXShot’s macOS app preferences

A project contains recording.mov, project.json, and steps/. Keep the entire package when moving or backing it up. Demo edits save automatically. Reset your personal settings with Restore Defaults (恢复默认设置) inside the app.

Prepare the screen before recording

  • Choose a window or area just large enough for the task to keep unrelated content out of the recording.
  • Silence notifications that may expose private information, and check browser tabs, file names, and account details.
  • Use demo data suitable for sharing. Sensitive information outside password fields may still be captured.

Sensitive information in recordings is not currently masked automatically. The screenshot editor’s Mosaic tool is manual and does not automatically protect video or step screenshots.

Review exports before sharing

Play the MP4 or click through every HTML step to check images, titles, and descriptions. HTML embeds full step images, which recipients can view. Offline playback does not mean the content has been anonymized.

Share the exported MP4 or HTML when someone only needs to view the result. Share a complete project package only when they need to edit it; the project also contains the original video and material outside the trimmed range.

The current HTML demo does not connect to or operate the product shown. It uses screenshots and hotspots and plays without a server. See exports and local projects for the format differences.

Read the source and report issues

XShot is licensed under MIT. Visit the GitHub repository to inspect the implementation, report an issue, or contribute. Remove private content from screenshots and projects before posting a public report.
